tagline: A winding mountain crossing follows Topanga Creek inland from the Pacific.
intro: Topanga Canyon Boulevard winds through the Santa Monica Mountains, linking the Pacific coast with the San Fernando Valley. Its southern portion largely follows Topanga Creek and cuts through Topanga State Park. Caltrans has officially designated a portion through Topanga Canyon as a scenic highway. The canyon landscape includes coastal sage, chaparral and California oak woodland. It is also a commuter crossing: drivers from the western San Fernando Valley use SR 27 to reach Santa Monica or Interstate 10.

The state highway system included a route from near Topanga Beach toward Chatsworth in 1933; two years later it became Route 156. The 1964 state highway renumbering gave it the SR 27 number. Mountain terrain has interrupted that connection: in January 2005, a 300-ton boulder landed on the boulevard and blocked through traffic for around a week. Crews drilled six-foot holes and used low-yield explosives to break the boulder apart after an earlier dynamite attempt failed because the rock was saturated with rain.

From the coast, the route starts at Pacific Coast Highway near Topanga State Beach and heads north through the park. It reaches Fernwood and Topanga, then continues winding toward Woodland Hills. Beyond the mountain crossing, the highway becomes a major city arterial through the valley and eventually reaches SR 118 at Chatsworth.

moments.title: Topanga State Beach
moments.text: Topanga Beach sits at the mouth of Topanga Canyon, where Topanga Creek reaches the coast. In the early 1900s, the area was a Japanese fishing village; in the 1960s and 1970s, it became an enclave of artists and surfers. Will Rogers State Beach borders it to the east, with Las Tunas Beach to the west. Here, near the Pacific, SR 27 begins its northward trip from Pacific Coast Highway into the canyon.

moments.title: Topanga Creek
moments.text: The southern part of Topanga Canyon Boulevard largely follows Topanga Creek, one of the area’s few remaining undammed waterways. The creek drains Topanga Canyon and provides spawning habitat for steelhead trout. Its outlet is at Topanga Beach. The creek also figured in the canyon’s development as a retreat from Los Angeles: in the 1920s, summer cabins were built along it and in subdivisions in the surrounding hills.

moments.title: Topanga
moments.text: The community occupies both Topanga Canyon and its surrounding hills in the Santa Monica Mountains, with the boulevard as its principal thoroughfare. In the 1950s, blacklisted actor Will Geer sold his Santa Monica home and moved his family to a small canyon plot where they could grow produce. Woody Guthrie had a shack on the property, and an artists’ colony developed unintentionally. The Geer family has operated the Will Geer Theatricum Botanicum since its founding in 1973. The theater occupies a natural outdoor amphitheater, with a repertoire that includes Shakespeare, modern classics, original productions and concerts.
